builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: A$^2$-VLA: Adapting Vision-Language-Action Policies to New Tools through Agentic Affordance Discovery
summary: A²-VLA replaces manual affordance engineering and per-tool retraining of vision-language-action policies with an agent that hypothesizes task-relevant affordance features, validates them through autonomous simulation experiments, and conditions a π0.5 backbone on the extracted functional-region features. It costs teleoperated demonstrations per source tool, a simulation reconstruction pipeline, an autonomous experiment loop for skill refinement, and fine-tuning of the π0.5 backbone, all of which exceed a single-GPU budget once robot hardware is included. It can fail when reconstructed scenes diverge from real geometry, when affordance hypotheses do not transfer to tools with novel functional regions, or when the accumulated skill library biases extraction toward previously seen tool categories.
rationale: The method requires teleoperated demonstrations, simulation scene reconstruction, and physical robot hardware that the reader's constrained infrastructure does not provide, so it is relevant to track but not adoptable for typical production LLM work.
technique: Agentic affordance discovery for cross-tool VLA adaptation

It costs teleoperated demonstrations per source tool, a simulation reconstruction pipeline, an autonomous experiment loop for skill refinement, and fine-tuning of the π0.5 backbone, all of which exceed a single-GPU budget once robot hardware is included. It can fail when reconstructed scenes diverge from real geometry, when affordance hypotheses do not transfer to tools with novel functional regions, or when the accumulated skill library biases extraction toward previously seen tool categories.
86.1% success in simulated cross-tool trajectory retargeting; +30.7 percentage points task success over a π0.5 baseline on three real-robot tool-use tasks.
